rationale: Existing force-or-fear robbery choices preserve degree distinctions. Attempted robbery is not a substitute for the completed offense.
Existing vehicle taking from possession or immediate presence by force or fear; temporary or permanent deprivation is preserved.
Existing burglary choices distinguish inhabited-location first degree from other burglary and the separate shoplifting rule.
Existing open-business-hours entry and $950 threshold; specified priors and repeat-theft allegations remain conditional.
Existing 496(a) receiving/concealing/withholding choice requires knowledge; dealer-inquiry duties are not silently substituted.

Existing petty-theft summary establishes value/grading limits, but does not itself complete the taking, movement, consent and deprivation alternatives. Reuse it; review the conduct wording before claiming detailed larceny coverage.

Section overlap does not establish reliance, transfer of ownership or corroboration for false-pretense theft. Improve the existing broad choice or supply bounded guidance without duplicating generic petty theft.
Section overlap does not establish the fraud-induced possession versus ownership distinction for theft by trick. Preserve this as substantive branch work.
Existing fraudulent appropriation of entrusted property under 503; punishment and public-funds exceptions remain bounded.
The existing 470 summary includes unauthorized signatures and intent to defraud; signing authority and the charged instrument still require branch-specific consideration.
Endorsement is an unauthorized-signature application of 470(a); reuse the existing summary without treating all signatures as unauthorized.
Existing summary expressly includes counterfeiting handwriting or seals, with intent to defraud.
Existing falsified-record summary supplies a broad choice; wills, court records and other specified legal writings must retain their document-specific limits.
Existing making/altering false-instrument summary applies only to qualifying writings; the seven-instrument $950 rule is not universal.
Existing passing-instrument summary preserves knowledge and intent to defraud; this is not a finding that possession alone proves passing or attempted use.
Existing 484g summary covers unauthorized/fraudulent use with intent to defraud; knowledge, card/account status and six-month aggregation remain relevant.
Existing 484g summary includes fraudulent holder representation. This does not silently substitute card possession or another 484e offense.
Existing insufficient-funds choice preserves willfulness, knowledge, fraudulent intent and outstanding instruments. Prior-conviction exceptions remain distinct; a bounced check alone is insufficient.
Existing unlawful-use choice under 530.5(a), not the separately reviewed possession-with-fraud-intent branch.
Existing 148(a)(1) choice preserves lawful performance and lawful-recording protection; weapon-taking subdivisions remain separate.
Courthouse picketing remains withheld pending constitutional/application research; this is a deliberate deferral, not cleared coverage.
Existing malicious damage/defacement choice preserves property ownership, value and prior-conviction conditions.
The 647(f) public-intoxication and 647(b) prostitution choices do not cover 647(h) loitering. Do not accept a shared section number as a match.
The existing 647(f)/(b) choices do not cover 647(i) peeking; verify the distinct conduct and exceptions before publication.
School loitering remains unpublished while the conduct-construction issue is unresolved. Retain the existing finding and avoid treating mere presence as sufficient.
Existing animal cruelty is 597(b). It does not establish the distinct malicious maiming/torture/wounding/killing branch in 597(a); prioritize that meaningful gap.
Existing under-21 public possession choice includes statutory exceptions and medical-assistance immunity; supplying alcohol is a different charge.
Existing 647(f) summary requires inability to care for safety or obstruction of a public way; neither ordinary intoxication nor other 647 subdivisions suffice.
Existing 270 summary and recorded attorney decision are reused; first/subsequent-offense uncertainty remains explicit, not reopened or treated as resolved.
Existing 186.10 choice preserves financial-institution transactions, seven/thirty-day thresholds and required knowledge or intent.
Existing own-recognizance misdemeanor/felony choices remain distinct from bail-related failure to appear; the 14-day presumption is not a grace period.
